title: Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs poached in spiced tomato and pepper sauce
excerpt: Eggs cracked into a bubbling sauce of tomatoes, peppers, onion, and cumin, then covered and cooked until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny. A North African and Middle Eastern dish eaten for breakfast, brunch, or any meal of the day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shakshuka is found across North Africa and the Middle East, with strong associations with Tunisia, Libya, Israel, and Yemen. The word is thought to derive from an Arabic root meaning to shake or to mix. The dish was brought to Israel in large numbers by North African and Yemeni Jews and is now a staple of Israeli café culture, often eaten for breakfast. The tomato-based version is the most widely known, though green and white versions using tomatillos, spinach, or labneh exist. The key technique is keeping the yolks soft while the whites set fully.

recipeTools.notes: Wide frying pan with a lid, or a shallow casserole dish that can go on the hob.

content.text: The sauce needs to be thick enough so the eggs sit in distinct wells rather than swimming. If the sauce is too thin, cook it for longer before adding the eggs. Make a well in the sauce with a spoon before cracking each egg in: this keeps the eggs in place while they set. Cover the pan after adding the eggs and do not peek for the first 3 minutes. The eggs are done when the whites are completely set but the yolks still wobble when you shake the pan gently.

Heat the olive oil in a large, wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the red pepper and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, smoked paprika, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and season. Crush the tomatoes with a spoon. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and reduced. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Make 6 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon. Crack an egg into each well. Cover the pan with a lid and cook on medium-low heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with fresh coriander or parsley and, if using, crumbled feta. Serve directly from the pan with crusty bread or pitta.
